bullets: Extending the output range of a precision VI (voltage-current) source-measure card from ±50 V to ±100 V at 200 mA, owning the high-voltage output stage from LTspice model to protoboard bring-up.

Designed a cascode output stage so no single MOSFET absorbs the full 200 V rail-to-rail swing at 200 mA: stacking devices in series splits the drain-source voltage and divides the resulting power dissipation between them, keeping each device inside V_DS and thermal limits the single-device topology could not meet. Selected the supporting high-voltage set, including complementary MOSFET pairs, 300 V-class BJTs, precision op-amps, and decoupling capacitors re-rated from 50 V to the 250 to 500 V class.

Recalculated the DC biasing network for the doubled rail, re-deriving operating points across the Class AB stage, cascode devices, and Zener/BJT bias spreader so every active device stays in its linear region across the full swing, then verified both feedback paths hold at the extremes: voltage feedback reports what the DUT actually receives at the pin, and current feedback clamps delivery at the IDAC-programmed limit.

Verified all designs in LTspice across the full swing, automating the regression testing in Python (PyLTSpice) to sweep DC input across schematic revisions and flag divergence by percent-difference tolerance. Traced a DC operating point convergence failure that had blocked simulation of the stage entirely to floating nodes in the negative pull-down sub-circuit.

Characterized the original ±50 V card on Credence TMT ASL1000 production ATE to establish the performance baseline for the extension, then correlated protoboard measurements of the extended design against simulation, resolving a floating MOSFET gate that produced phantom DMM readings and a V_GS mismatch against the simulated bias point.
